verification: Live W&M catalog opened and read through Codex in-app browser; program requirements tabs and undergraduate CSCI/MATH course descriptions.

offering_policy.statement: The current CSCI and relevant MATH catalog course descriptions do not provide recurring fall/spring/summer offering patterns. Show “Not stated in catalog” rather than inferred common semesters.
offering_policy.registration_caveat: Catalog descriptions and requirements do not establish a future section schedule.

programs.name: Computer Science, Minor
programs.credit_note: Catalog states 18–19 depending on credit awarded for CSCI 141; current course listing assigns CSCI 141 four credits.

requirements.label: Upper-level electives
requirements.course_rule: Choose 9 credits from 300–400 level Computer Science courses excluding CSCI 320, CSCI 430, CSCI 498. MATH 413 and MATH 414 may count toward partial fulfillment.

career_fit_inference.text: Add programming, data structures, and discrete reasoning to another primary field; upper-level electives can deepen a chosen computing interest.
career_fit_inference.status: Interpretation of curriculum, not a placement or employment claim.

programs.name: Computer Science (BS in Computer Science)
programs.required_credit_hours_display: 36–37 major credits; catalog table 48–51 including mathematics proficiency
programs.credit_note: Catalog header states 36–37 major credits depending on CSCI 141 credit. The requirements table totals 48–51 including math proficiency: current 25-credit CS core + 12 elective credits + 11 math credits, and 3 additional probability/statistics proficiency credits for AI/ML. The MATH 109 course description also requires the 1-credit MATH 109L corequisite; that lab is not listed in the CS program table.
programs.writing_requirement: Successful completion of the major core requirements.
programs.catalog_planning_guidance: By the end of sophomore year, intended majors are encouraged to complete CSCI 141, 241, 243 (or MATH 214), one required 300-level CS course, and the required calculus and linear algebra proficiencies.
residency_rules: At least half of the minimum required number of CS major courses must be taken at W&M.
At most two 300/400-level courses taken elsewhere may count toward the CS major.

catalog_ambiguities: Credit scope differs by catalog display: header 36–37 for major; table 48–51 including mathematics proficiency. Explain the scopes explicitly instead of presenting either as total degree credits.
MATH 109 requires MATH 109L in the course description; the CS program table lists only MATH 109.

Both CSCI 315 and CSCI 415 (Systems Programming), CSCI 321 and CSCI 421 (Database Systems), and CSCI 412 and CSCI 432 (Web Programming) appear as separate current catalog entries. No course-number equivalence is assumed.
Catalog rules broadly allow 300–400 CSCI electives, but sections, prerequisites, research permissions, Honors admission, and duplicate credit need advising review.
